extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, patent examiners, and biological depository administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for making, maintaining, replacing, and documenting deposits of biological material for U.S. patent applications and patents (37 CFR §§1.803–1.809; MPEP §2400 series). Covers depository suitability, timing, viability, term, access, replacement procedures, and examination treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depository suitability/recognition (37 CFR 1.803)
rubrics_metrics.description: A depository will be recognized as acceptable if it is either an International Depositary Authority (IDA) under the Budapest Treaty, or is recognized as suitable by the Commissioner. Suitability is judged by the Commissioner based on need and information supplied by the organization seeking status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office generally will not recognize organizations where need is already met by IDAs. The Office prefers an independent depository (not under control of the depositor) to ensure continued availability and to protect the public interest; notice of recognition/default/discontinuance will be published in the Official Gazette. Applicants should follow 37 CFR 1.803(a)(2) and (b) when seeking recognition of a depository.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time of making an original deposit (37 CFR 1.804)
rubrics_metrics.description: An original deposit of a biological material specifically identified in an application may be made any time before filing the application or, subject to §1.809, during pendency of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended to deposit before filing. If deposit is made after the effective filing date, applicant must promptly submit corroboration per §1.804(b). If deposit is needed to satisfy 35 U.S.C.112 and made during pendency, it must be made no later than the time set by the examiner (e.g., by the notice of allowance deadline). Post-issuance original deposits are not permitted; cannot cure lack of original deposit by reissue or reexamination in most cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific identification in application (37 CFR 1.804(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The biological material deposited must be specifically identified in the application for patent as filed to meet the description requirement of 35 U.S.C.112 and provide antecedent basis for the deposited material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specification should clearly show the invention was capable of reduction to practice; adding depository, accession number, and deposit date after filing may be permissible (see Lundak example) but the application as filed must make clear the material is described/claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corroboration when deposit made after filing (37 CFR 1.804(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: When an original deposit is made after the effective filing date, the applicant must promptly submit a statement from a person in a position to corroborate that the deposited material is the one specifically identified in the application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The necessary nature and form of corroboration depends on circumstances (length of time between filing and deposit, evidence). While rare, situations where the material did not exist at filing are not categorically precluded, but satisfying description enablement is difficult.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign priority caution re: deposit timing (MPEP §2406.03)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants intending to file outside the U.S. relying on a deposit should note many countries require the deposit to be made before the filing date of the priority application to obtain foreign priority rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A deposit made after the U.S. filing date may comply with U.S. 35 U.S.C.112 but may forfeit foreign priority in some jurisdictions. Plan deposit timing accordingly for international filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement or supplemental deposit trigger and notification (37 CFR 1.805(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A depositor, upon learning during pendency (or in certain post-grant proceedings) that the depository cannot furnish samples or that the deposit is contaminated or lost capability, must notify the Office in writing for each affected application/patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether replacement/supplement is needed is governed by the same considerations as original deposits (§1.802(b)). Replacement/supplement made during pendency will not be accepted unless it meets original deposit requirements (including §1.804(b) corroboration if after filing). For patents, replacement/supplement generally requires requesting a certificate of correction meeting §§1.805(b) and (c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of correction content for replacement/supplement (37 CFR 1.805(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A certificate of correction under this section shall identify: (1) the accession number for the replacement or supplemental deposit; (2) the date of the deposit; and (3) the name and address of the depository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items must be included in the certificate of correction request for the Office to grant the correction associated with a replacement/supplement deposit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of correction request requirements (37 CFR 1.805(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for a certificate of correction must be made promptly after replacement/supplemental deposit and must include: reason for replacement/supplement; a corroborating statement that the replacement is identical to the original; a showing that the patent owner acted diligently; a statement that the term of the replacement/supplement expires no earlier than the original; and otherwise establish compliance with the regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diligence showing differs for replacement (deposit after notice that samples could not be furnished) vs supplemental (after notice of contamination or loss of capability). Promptness and robust corroboration are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failure to replace (37 CFR 1.805(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to replace a deposit, or to diligently replace and promptly request a certificate of correction after being notified that samples cannot be furnished, will cause the application or patent to be treated in any Office proceeding as if no deposit were made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This can be fatal to meeting 35 U.S.C.112 requirements if the deposit was necessary; applicants/patent owners must act promptly when notified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttable presumption of identity for replacement deposit (37 CFR 1.805(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: When a deposit is replaced according to regulations, the Office will apply a rebuttable presumption that the replacement deposit is identical to the original deposit in any Office proceeding where a patent referencing the deposit is relied upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner will assume the replacement provides the same material unless evidence to the contrary is presented. Replacement during pendency may be made for any reason and is not held to a higher standard than an original deposit made during pendency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions from replacement (37 CFR 1.805(g),(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: No replacement/supplemental deposit is necessary where the biological material need not be deposited under §1.802(b), or where the depository can furnish samples but cannot provide them to requesters outside its jurisdiction for national security, health, or environmental safety reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 5 of the Budapest Treaty and national law may permit certain accessibility restrictions; the Office recognizes limited exemptions but otherwise treats inability to furnish samples as triggering replacement duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement not recognized if original still furnishable (37 CFR 1.805(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will not recognize in any Office proceeding a replacement deposit made by a patent owner where the depository could furnish samples of the deposit being replaced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best evidence of what was originally deposited should not be lost through destruction or replacement if the original deposit remains capable of furnishing samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of deposit (37 CFR 1.806)
rubrics_metrics.description: A deposit made before or during pendency shall be made for a term of at least thirty (30) years and at least five (5) years after the most recent request for a sample; samples must be stored under agreements to make them available beyond the enforceable life of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term must satisfy Budapest Treaty requirements. If the 30-year term measured from deposit would terminate within the enforceable life of the patent (patent term plus statute of limitations), then storage agreements ensuring availability beyond patent life are required. Applicants must indicate the term unless deposit is under the Budapest Treaty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viability requirement for self-replicating deposits (37 CFR 1.807(a)-(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A deposit of biological material capable of self-replication must be viable at time of deposit and during the term; viability may be tested by the depository and a viability statement must be filed if not made under the Budapest Treaty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Viability test need only show capability of reproduction, not functional performance. For non-Budapest deposits, viability statement must include (1) depository name/address, (2) depositor name/address, (3) date of deposit, (4) identity and accession number, (5) date of viability test, (6) procedures used to obtain sample if test not done by depository, and (7) statement that deposit is capable of reproduction. Examiner will proceed as if no deposit were made if viability test shows non-viable or examiner cannot accept applicant's statement for valid reasons. Examiner accepts viability conclusions issued by recognized depositories under §1.803(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Furnishing of samples and access conditions (37 CFR 1.808)
rubrics_metrics.description: A deposit must be made under conditions assuring (a) access during pendency to persons entitled under §1.14 and 35 U.S.C.122, and (b) except as permitted in §1.808(b), irrevocable removal of depositor-imposed restrictions upon grant of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted contractual restrictions (§1.808(b)) allow the depositor to require that samples be furnished only if: (1) request is in writing/dated; (2) request contains name/address of requesting party and accession number; and (3) depository communicates the request in writing to the depositor with date and recipient details. These exceptions must be strictly followed; no variations are accepted. Upon request to the Office with specified information, the Office will certify whether a deposit was stated to have been made under conditions making it available as of issue date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions of deposit strictness and Budapest Treaty interplay (MPEP 2410.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: The two required deposit conditions—access during pendency to entitled persons and removal of restrictions upon grant (except the narrow §1.808(b) exception)—must be strictly followed. Indication a deposit was made and accepted under the Budapest Treaty will generally satisfy conditions except the specific removal-of-restrictions requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National law may permit other conditions under the Budapest Treaty; however, U.S. rules require strict compliance with the stated exception. Mere statement of deposit acceptance without details may be insufficient to show compliance with 35 U.S.C.112.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of statement of availability of deposit (MPEP 2410.02)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon request to a Director of Technology Center (TC) 1600, the Office will certify whether a deposit has been stated to have been made under conditions making it available to the public as of the issue date, provided the request contains: depository name/address, accession number, patent number and issue date, and name/address of requesting party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must be made to TC1600 Director's office (not via the examiner). The Office will not certify availability until a U.S. patent referencing the deposit has issued. For Budapest Treaty deposits, WIPO Form BP-12 and related guidance may be used to request certification of legal entitlement to receive samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination procedures—when deposit is needed and acceptability (37 CFR 1.809(a)-(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner shall determine in each application/reexamination/reissue if a deposit is needed and, if needed, whether a deposit made is acceptable for patent purposes. If a needed deposit has not been made or is unacceptable, the examiner shall reject affected claims under appropriate provision(s) of 35 U.S.C.112 explaining why a deposit is needed and/or why the deposit cannot be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant/patent owner must reply by making an acceptable original/replacement/supplemental deposit or assuring the Office in writing that an acceptable deposit will be made, or arguing why a deposit is not needed or should be accepted. Other replies are nonresponsive and the rejection will be repeated until satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for making deposit after notice of allowability (37 CFR 1.809(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is otherwise in condition for allowance except for a needed deposit and the Office has received a written assurance that an acceptable deposit will be made, the Office may set a three month period from mailing date of the notice of allowability within which the deposit must be made to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This three-month period is not extendable under §1.136 (see §1.136(c)); applicants must meet the deadline or risk abandonment. Written assurance must provide sufficiently detailed information to convince the examiner no outstanding deposit issues remain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification content required for each deposit (37 CFR 1.809(d)-(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each deposit made pursuant to the regulations, the specification must contain: (1) the accession number for the deposit; (2) the date of the deposit; (3) a description sufficient to specifically identify the deposited biological material and permit examination; and (4) the name and address of the depository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any amendment required to add or correct accession number, deposit date, or depository name/address must be filed before or with payment of the issue fee. See MPEP §2404.01 for guidance on description sufficient for examination.
